features.text: The patient is 28 years old and male.
The patient has been experiencing neck pain since a car accident a week ago.
The neck pain is located in the back of the neck and is not constant, worsening with head movement.
The neck pain is rated as seven out of ten in severity.
The patient has experienced headaches early on but no numbness, tingling, or weakness.
The patient has not undergone any imaging studies or consulted a specialist for the neck pain.
The patient tried ibuprofen, which provided some relief.
The patient has not had an MRI yet and is still waiting for the results.
The patient was wearing a seatbelt during the car accident, and their head and neck were jerked forward quickly.
The patient did not lose consciousness during the car accident but felt sudden pain afterward.
The patient has no history of neck injuries or surgeries other than the car accident.
The patient has not experienced any balance issues, dizziness, or changes in vision since the accident.
The patient has not experienced radiation of pain to the arms, shoulders, or upper back.
The patient has difficulty moving their head, particularly turning it side to side or bending it back.
The patient can still manage most of their daily activities despite the neck pain.
The patient has not experienced any changes in the severity of neck pain over the past week.
The patient has not experienced any new neurological symptoms such as numbness, tingling, or weakness in the arms or legs.
